## 📋 Spec ready for review — Gate 1 of the SDD workflow

- **Feature directory**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`
- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist**: all items pass (`checklists/requirements.md`)

Here's the essence of what I've specified for your approval. Per our workflow, **nothing gets planned or built until you sign off on this.**

### What the app does (in plain terms)
An app to **save web links and manage them over time**. Four prioritized slices, each usable on its own:

| Priority | Capability |
|----------|------------|
| **P1** | Save a bookmark by URL (auto-grabs the page title), with duplicate protection |
| **P1** | Browse the saved list and open any bookmark in the browser |
| **P2** | Edit and delete bookmarks (delete asks for confirmation) |
| **P2** | Organize with tags; search and filter to find things fast |

The P1 pair alone is a working minimum product; P2 makes a growing collection manageable.

### What I've assumed (so you can correct me)
- **Single user, stored locally** — no accounts, cloud sync, or sharing in v1.
- Web links only (http/https).
- Importing/exporting existing browser bookmarks is **out of scope for v1**.

### One question that meaningfully changes scope

**How should bookmarks be stored and accessed?**

| Option | Answer | Implications |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| **A** | Single user, local only (my default) | Simplest; fast to build. No login, no sync — bookmarks live on one device. |
| **B** | Single user, but synced across their devices | Adds a sync/storage backend and more moving parts; no multi-user complexity. |
| **C** | Multiple users with accounts | Adds sign-up, login, and per-user isolation — significantly larger scope. |
| **Custom** | Describe it | e.g. "browser extension", "shared team collection", etc. |

---

**Please review the spec** (open `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` for the full detail) and let me know:
1. Your answer to the scope question above, and
2. Any changes to the stories, requirements, or assumptions.

Once you approve, I'll move to **Gate 2: the implementation plan** (`/speckit-plan`). Would you also like me to run `/speckit-clarify` first if anything else feels ambiguous?

This looks like a really solid start — thank you for laying it out so clearly. Let me go through it.

**On the scope question: Option A.** Just me, on my own machine, no logins or accounts. That's exactly what I want for now.

A few things I want to flag or adjust:

**The duplicate thing isn't quite what I pictured.** You've got it telling me "this is already saved." That's fine as far as it goes, but what I'd actually want is: if I try to save a link I've already got, it just takes me straight to that existing bookmark so I can tweak it — update its note, add a tag, whatever. Basically treat the second save as "let me edit the one I already have," not a dead end.

**Searching should look inside my notes too.** You've got search covering the title, address, and tags — but if I've jotted a note on a bookmark, I'd expect searching a word from that note to find it. And searching shouldn't care about capital letters — "Recipe" and "recipe" should turn up the same things.

**When I save something, grab a bit more than just the title.** The little site icons (the favicon) would help me a lot when I'm scanning the list — I recognize sites by their icon faster than by reading. And if the page has a short description, pulling that in automatically would be nice too (I can always edit it).

**Sorting by more than just newest.** Ordering by most-recently-added is good as a default, but I'd like to be able to flip it to sort alphabetically by title when I'm hunting for something.

**When I type a tag, suggest ones I've already used.** Otherwise I'll end up with "recipes" and "recipe" and "cooking" all meaning the same thing. Show me my existing tags as I type.

**One I'd push back on:** you've put importing my existing browser bookmarks out of scope. I get keeping v1 small, but honestly I've already got a pile of bookmarks in my browser — being able to bring those in matters to me. Could we keep that on the table rather than cutting it?

The stories, the empty states, the delete confirmation, the invalid-address handling — all of that reads right to me. No need to run the extra clarify step; I think the above covers what was nagging at me.

## 📐 Implementation plan ready — Gate 2 of the SDD workflow

Generated artifacts in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`:
- **plan.md** — technical approach, stack, structure
- **research.md** — 9 key decisions with rationale + rejected alternatives
- **data-model.md** — Bookmark / Tag entities, search index, traceability to requirements
- **contracts/api.md** — the local REST API the UI talks to
- **quickstart.md** — how to run it + a validation checklist mapped to every story

### The plan in plain terms

**What it is:** a small program you run on your own machine and use through your web browser. Everything stays local — your bookmarks live in a single file on your computer, no accounts, no cloud.

**The one decision worth explaining:** the app needs a small "backend" running locally, not just a page in the browser. Three of your requirements force this — the browser (for security reasons) *cannot* fetch other sites' titles/icons, and it can't read or write the bookmark files that browsers import/export. A local backend does all three cleanly. It also means your data sits in one portable file you can copy or back up anytime — reinforcing the no-lock-in point you cared about.

**Key choices and why:**

| Area | Choice | Why it serves what you asked for |
|------|--------|-------------------------------|
| Storage | A local database file | Handles thousands of bookmarks with instant search; trivially backed up/moved |
| Metadata on save | Best-effort, time-limited fetch | Grabs title/icon/description but never makes you wait on a slow site |
| Favicons | Saved locally at save-time | Icons show instantly, work offline, don't "phone home" every time you scroll |
| Import/export | Standard browser bookmark format | Your existing folders → tags, original dates kept; exports re-open in any browser |
| Notes | Small formatting toolbar (links/bold/bullets), cleaned for safety | Exactly the "keep a note readable" scope you wanted |

**Build order** follows your priorities: the P1 core (save + browse) is a working app on its own; tags/search, then import/export come after.

---

All 48 tasks through US5 are complete; 37 tests pass. No extension hooks. Stopping here for you to try import on your real file, exactly as you asked.

## ✅ US5 (Import) built and verified

**What's new:**
- An **"Import browser bookmarks"** button in the header (top-right).
- It reads a standard browser export (`bookmarks.html` from Chrome/Firefox/Edge/Safari) and:
  - Brings in every bookmark's **title and address**
  - Turns **folders into tags** — nested folders add a tag per level
  - **Keeps each bookmark's original date**, so newest-first stays meaningful
  - **Skips anything already saved**, and tells you *"Imported N, skipped M already saved"*
  - **Rejects a non-bookmark file** with a clear message and imports nothing
